detaileddescription.para: This page describes the primary data structures and representations used in HighMap.

sect1.title: 1. Elevation Representations
sect1.para: HighMap provides three main structures for 2D height data:

entry.para: In-memory 2D array of floats with contiguous storage.
Tiled 2D array designed for parallel computation.
Tiled structure supporting disk and RAM storage for large grids.

sect2.title: Array
sect2.para: Array is the basic container for 2D elevation fields. Data is stored in row-major order. It supports arithmetic operators, statistical queries, slicing, and filtering.

sect1.title: 2. Bivariate Functions
sect1.para: Continuous functions deriving from hmap::Function represent mathematical surfaces $f(x, y)$ independently of resolution:

listitem.para: hmap::NoiseFunction: Perlin, Simplex, and cellular noise generators.
hmap::FieldFunction: Distance fields and geometric functions.

sect1.title: 3. Geometric Primitives
sect1.para: Geometric entities represent vector features and integrate with height arrays:

listitem.para: hmap::Point / hmap::Cloud: Individual points and point clouds.
hmap::Edge / hmap::Path: Segments and ordered sequences of points.
hmap::Graph: Node and edge graphs used for networks such as rivers and roads.

sect1.title: 4. Talus vs. Slope
sect1.para: When simulating erosion or analyzing terrain gradients, HighMap distinguishes between talus and slope:

sect2.title: Talus (Grid-Space Elevation Difference)
sect2.para: In HighMap, the talus is defined as the direct elevation difference between neighboring grid cells (or the critical vertical threshold per grid step):

listitem.para: Resolution dependent: For a given physical terrain gradient, increasing the grid resolution $N_x \times N_y$ places adjacent cell centers closer together, decreasing the elevation step $\Delta z$ between neighbors. Consequently, threshold talus parameters scale inversely with grid resolution (e.g., $\text{talus} \propto 1 / N_x$).
Domain size independent: Talus operates entirely in discrete grid space ($i, j$) and does not depend on the physical world-space dimensions of the terrain domain.

sect2.title: Slope (Metric Surface Gradient)
sect2.para: The slope is the metric rate of change of elevation with respect to physical horizontal distance in the terrain domain:
where $\Delta x = L_x / N_x$ represents the physical cell spacing for a domain of size $L_x$.

listitem.para: Domain size dependent: Slope depends on physical metric units (such as meters or kilometers) and the overall domain extent $L_x \times L_y$.

Resolution independent: As grid resolution increases ($N_x \to \infty$), the ratio $\Delta z / \Delta x$ converges toward the continuous spatial derivative $|\nabla z|$, maintaining an invariant physical slope regardless of raster resolution.

sect1.title: 5. Scattering
sect1.para: The scattering system handles the distribution of discrete objects over a terrain:

listitem.para: hmap::ScatterItem: Basic element storing a 3D position, an integer class identifier, and a radius.
hmap::ScatterField: Container providing spatial operations (collision pruning, density maps, elevation projection).
hmap::Forest: Scattering container for vegetation and growth models.
hmap::RockField: Scattering container for rock and debris placement.
